Interface FormParts

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
public interface FormParts extends AutoCloseable
The parts of a submitted form, application/x-www-form-urlencoded or multipart/form-data, read forward as they arrive, like a cursor. Nothing is buffered: each part is handed to a consumer, and a part that is skipped or not read is discarded.

Read every part:

routes.asyncPOST("/upload", (request, pathVariables, body) -> body.parts()
    .forEach(part -> part.isFile()
            ? part.file().transferTo(uploads.resolve(UUID.randomUUID().toString()))
            : part.text(8_192).thenAccept(value -> fields.put(part.name(), value)))
        .thenApply(done -> HttpResponse.ok()));

Or read only the parts that are needed, in the order the client sends them, and throw out the rest:

parts.part("title", part -> part.text(8_192).thenAccept(title::set))
    .thenCompose(found -> parts.part("avatar", part -> part.file().transferTo(path)))
    .thenCompose(found -> parts.closeAsync()
        .thenApply(closed -> found ? HttpResponse.noContent() : HttpResponse.badRequest()));

One operation at a time: start the next one when the stage of the previous one completed; the stage of an operation started while another one is in progress fails with an IllegalStateException: the operations report every failure through their stage, and do not throw. A consumer callback owns its part until the stage it returned completes; then what it did not consume is discarded, and the next part is only read once that is done. A callback that returns null fails the operation.

The end of the form and closing are different: at the end of the form, part(String, Function) completes with false and forEach(Function) completes normally, while closing the parts during an operation completes that operation with a CancellationException, and the stage of an operation started after closing fails with an IllegalStateException.

The parts of a FormParts argument, and those of AsyncRequestBody.parts(), are closed like the reads of an AsyncRequestBody: when the controller method or the request filter method completed, normally or exceptionally, before the response is written or the filter chain continues, or, for a controller method that answers with a streamed response, when its stream ended: completed, failed or was cancelled. An operation the method did not wait for is aborted then, so the stage of the work must be part of the stage the method returns. The parts of a request filter method consume the body, like AsyncRequestBody.parts(): the route fails when it reads the body after the filter read a part.

  • Method Details

    • forEach

      CompletionStage<Void> forEach(Function<? super FormPart, ? extends CompletionStage<?>> consumer)
      Consume the remaining parts of the form in the order they arrive. The next part is read when the stage returned for the previous one completes, and the content a consumer did not read is discarded.
      Parameters:
      consumer - Consumes a part, completing when it is done with it
      Returns:
      Completes when every remaining part is consumed, or exceptionally when reading the form or a consumer fails, with an IllegalStateException when another operation is in progress or the parts were closed, and with the cause when the form cannot be read, e.g. a body that was already read

    • part

      CompletionStage<Boolean> part(String name, Function<? super FormPart, ? extends CompletionStage<?>> consumer)
      Read forward to the next part with the given name and consume it. The parts before it are discarded, and the parts after it are left for the next operation: a part the client sent earlier than the current position is not found.
      Parameters:
      name - The name of the part
      consumer - Consumes the part, completing when it is done with it
      Returns:
      Completes with true when the part was consumed, false when the form ended without it, or exceptionally when reading the form or the consumer fails, like forEach(Function)

    • closeAsync

      CompletionStage<Void> closeAsync()
      Throw out the rest of the form without reading it, and discard the part a consumer holds. An operation that has not completed ends with a CancellationException. Closing again returns the same stage.
      Returns:
      Completes when the part a consumer held was released
